question: How can millions of strangers cooperate when chimpanzees can't manage more than a few dozen?
answer: Harari's answer: shared stories. Nations, money, laws and companies exist only because millions of people believe in them together. A chimp cannot be persuaded to give you a banana for a promise of bananas in heaven; humans trade, obey and fight for such shared fictions every day.
move: Much of what you obey exists because everyone agrees it does.
simply: A banknote is just paper. It works because everyone believes everyone else will accept it. Harari says nations and companies work the same way.
why: Seeing which things are shared agreements, money, borders, brands, helps you understand why they can change fast when belief changes.
reference: Yuval Noah Harari, Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind (Harper, 2015), ch. 2
